newsitem.title: USA: India wheat buying takes "breather" -- U.S. attache.
newsitem.headline: India wheat buying takes "breather" -- U.S. attache.

text.p: An agricultural attache posted at the U.S. embassy in New Dehli said India appears to have taken a "breather" after recent wheat purchases as the government assesses the impact on local and domestic prices.

"Some official sources have remarked that tendering may be complete until at least after harvest given potential logistical constraints, while rumors of a tender before Christmas are also making the rounds," the attache wrote in a report dated December 19.
The report was released by the U.S. Agriculture Department this week. Attache reports are not official USDA data.

"The most likely scenario seems to be that STC (the government-run State Trading Corporation) will wait until after the new year to review what impact news of the imports has had on domestic and international prices," the attache said.

The attache said Argentina is frequently mentioned as a possible origin for additional purchases, but said officials are unfamiliar with Argentine wheat and the STC may be reluctant to buy large volumes.
On Dec. 12, India said it would import two million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97 to increase domestic supplies and check rising prices. India last imported wheat four years ago.
Australia has sold 1.0 million tonnes of wheat to India.
The attache said trade sources indicate India also bought 250,000 tonnes from Canada at $152.50 FOB with an option for an additional 200,000 tonnes.
The attache also said flour millers are exploring import options.

"However, it seems increasingly unlikely that large volumes of wheat will be purchased by the private sector and 100,000 (tonnes) may be the upper limit for private sector purchases," the attache wrote.
